newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain farmers boost stocks over crop fear -ONIC.
newsitem.headline: EU grain farmers boost stocks over crop fear -ONIC.

text.p: Public grain stocks in the European Union are set to fall five percent at the end of this season, while the amount of grain held in private hands will jump by 34 percent over the previous year, according to a French report.

France's cereals office, ONIC, says high prices and fears over the next harvest have discouraged transfers of grain into EU intervention stores and left more than one million tonnes of extra grain kept back on the farm.
The EU's annual crop season ends on June 30.
On that date total stocks are seen 16 percent higher than a year previously at 28.3 million tonnes after a similar 16 percent rise in last year's harvests to 204.3 million tonnes.

Of the 3.8 million tonnes grain in stocks, 1.2 million will be on farm, 2.7 million, or 15 percent, in the private market, while public stocks will fall 100,000 tones or five percent over the previous year to 2.6 million tonnes.

"Because of high prices and possible difficulties with the next harvest, intervention stocks will remain limited, but stocks held by farmers will gain over a million tonnes," ONIC said in the first of a series of reports covering the whole EU.
ONIC said it had compiled the estimates from data available in the rest of the 15-nation EU as well as from its own sources.
It said most of the grain in EU intervention would be in Germany, where about half of the 2.1 million tonnes of grain previously bought from farmers at guaranteed prices would be rye.
Barley would account for nearly all the increase in grain held on farms. Farm storage would double to two million tonnes, or 25 percent of the total carried over between crop seasons.
"Expectations of difficult crops should encourage significant volumes to be kept on farm," ONIC said.
Early signs of drought in the spring raised fears of damage to various crops, though ONIC said on Wednesday recent rainfall had eased the problem in France except in the far south.
Overall barley stocks should rise 20 percent to 8.1 million tonnes, ONIC said, with 900,000 tonnes of that held in intervention and 5.3 million on the free market.
Stocks of soft wheat would rise nine percent to 9.8 million tonnes. Of this 1.6 million tonnes would be on farm, 7.6 million on the free market and 600,000 in EU silos.

Maize stocks would see the sharpest percentage rise, by 26 percent to 5.7 million tonnes, allowing it to regain some competitivity and achieve a smoother break between crop campaigns than last year, ONIC said.
The total would include 500,000 tonnes on farm and 5.2 million in the free market but zero in EU intervention. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
